The agent was stalled by a stream watchdog at the moment it was about to commit, so I committed its file on its behalf, then reviewed it. Independently verified the two load-bearing SDK claims: AccessToken.resource exists (provider.py:57) but every read is in the authorization-server handlers — nothing in bearer_auth.py (the resource-server request path) validates it, so RFC 8707 audience validation is genuinely not enforced; and IntrospectionTokenVerifier appears only in a docstring, not as shipped code. Recommendation: remain a pure resource server with WorkOS AuthKit as the AS. Claude.ai's CIMD/DCR behaviour is honestly flagged as unverified.

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text:
## SDK fact 1: `AuthSettings` fields (verified)

Installed `mcp` is **2.0.0** (`uv run python -c "from importlib.metadata import version; print(version('mcp'))"`).

Full field list, `.venv/lib64/python3.13/site-packages/mcp/server/auth/settings.py:15-42`:

| Field | Type | Default | Line |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issuer_url` | `AnyHttpUrl` | **required** | 22 |
| `service_documentation_url` | `AnyHttpUrl \| None` | `None` | 26 |
| `client_registration_options` | `ClientRegistrationOptions \| None` | `None` | 27 |
| `revocation_options` | `RevocationOptions \| None` | `None` | 28 |
| `required_scopes` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | 29 |
| `identity_assertion_enabled` | `bool` | `False` | 30 |
| `resource_server_url` | `AnyHttpUrl \| None` | **required** (`Field(...)`) | 38 |

Notes:
- `resource_server_url` is typed optional but declared `Field(...)` — i.e. **required but nullable**. Line 38.
- `model_config = ConfigDict(url_preserve_empty_path=True)` at line 20, with a comment confirming the trailing-slash/RFC-8414 reasoning already encoded in our `auth.py` docstring. Confirms the `model_validate` rule.
- **New in 2.0 and previously unknown to us:** `identity_assertion_enabled` (line 30-35) advertises the SEP-990 Identity Assertion Authorization Grant (RFC 7523 jwt-bearer carrying an ID-JAG) for enterprise IdP flows. Requires the provider to implement `exchange_identity_assertion`. Not needed for our case but worth knowing it exists.
- `ClientRegistrationOptions` (lines 4-8): `enabled: bool = False`, `client_secret_expiry_seconds`, `valid_scopes`, `default_scopes`. These are **AS-side** options (they gate the SDK's own /register endpoint), not RS-side.
- `RevocationOptions` (lines 11-12): just `enabled: bool = False`. Also AS-side.

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text:
## SDK fact 2: audience validation (RFC 8707) is NOT enforced by the SDK — **we must do it**

Traced the whole request path. Only two things gate a request:

1. `BearerAuthBackend.authenticate`, `mcp/server/auth/middleware/bearer_auth.py:47-66` — extracts the `Bearer ` header, calls `verify_token`, rejects on `None`, and rejects if `auth_info.expires_at < now` (lines 63-64). **That is all.**
2. `RequireAuthMiddleware.__call__`, `bearer_auth.py:93-111` — rejects 401 if no `AuthenticatedUser` in scope, then loops `required_scopes` and rejects 403 `insufficient_scope` if any is missing (103-109).

`AccessToken.resource` exists (`mcp/server/auth/provider.py:57`, commented `# RFC 8707 resource indicator`) but **nothing in the middleware ever reads it**. Verified by grep: no comparison of `resource` against `resource_server_url` anywhere in the request path.

### Consequence for the build beads

Our `TokenVerifier.verify_token` implementation **must itself** check that the token's audience matches our resource URL, and return `None` if not. Otherwise any token the chosen AS issued for *any* other resource in the same tenant would be accepted here — the confused-deputy problem RFC 8707 exists to prevent. This is a required acceptance criterion on the verifier bead, not a nice-to-have.

## SDK fact 3: `auth_server_provider=` is STILL PRESENT in 2.0.0 (not removed)

The task brief asked whether the deprecated own-AS parameter survives. It does:

- `MCPServer.__init__(..., auth_server_provider: OAuthAuthorizationServerProvider[Any, Any, Any] | None = None, token_verifier: TokenVerifier | None = None, ...)` — `mcp/server/mcpserver/server.py:157-158`.
- Mutual exclusion enforced at `server.py:237-242`: both → `ValueError("Cannot specify both auth_server_provider and token_verifier")`; neither with `auth` set → `ValueError("Must specify either ... when auth is enabled")`; either without `auth` → `ValueError("Cannot specify auth_server_provider or token_verifier without auth settings")`. Confirms the 'both must be given together' rule from lgmcp-07y.1.
- If a provider is given, the SDK wraps it: `self._token_verifier = ProviderTokenVerifier(auth_server_provider)` (`server.py:248-249`), described at `provider.py:358-363` as "provided for backwards compatibility with existing auth_server_provider".

So the SDK *can* still act as its own AS. That keeps the self-hosted option technically open.

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text:
## SDK fact 4: prototype run — RS mode works, output captured

Ran a throwaway spike (`tmp/oauth_spike.py`, not committed): `MCPServer(token_verifier=..., auth=AuthSettings.model_validate({...}))` + `streamable_http_app()`, driven with `starlette.testclient.TestClient`. Issuer `https://lgsf.example.auth0.com`, resource `https://lgsf-mcp.tail1234.ts.net/mcp`.

**Routes registered (only two):** `/mcp` and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`.

**`GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` → 200**, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`:

```json
{
  "resource": "https://lgsf-mcp.tail1234.ts.net/mcp",
  "authorization_servers": ["https://lgsf.example.auth0.com"],
  "scopes_supported": ["lgsf:read"],
  "bearer_methods_supported": ["header"]
}
```

**Unauthenticated `POST /mcp` → 401** with

```
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="Authentication required", resource_metadata="https://lgsf-mcp.tail1234.ts.net/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"
```

**`GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` → 404.** Expected and important: in pure RS mode the SDK serves *no* AS metadata. That document is the AS's job, not ours.

Confirms:
- No trailing slash on either URL — `model_validate` did its job.
- `scopes_supported` in the RS metadata is populated from `required_scopes` (`lowlevel/server.py:821`), so those two are the same list; you cannot advertise a scope you don't require.
- `authorization_servers` is exactly `[issuer_url]` — a **single-element** list, hardcoded at `lowlevel/server.py:820`. No way to advertise multiple ASes through `AuthSettings`.
- The 401 `resource_metadata=` pointer is built by `build_resource_metadata_url` (`auth/routes.py:202-217`), which splices `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` between host and path per RFC 9728 §3.1.

## SDK fact 5: `IntrospectionTokenVerifier` is NOT in the installed wheel

`find .venv -path '*simple-auth*'` → nothing. `grep -rn IntrospectionTokenVerifier` across `site-packages/mcp/` hits **only a docstring reference** at `provider.py:363`. `bearer_auth.py:34` likewise points at `examples/servers/simple-auth/mcp_simple_auth/token_verifier.py` — a path in the SDK's **git repo**, not in the distributed package.

So there is no importable introspection verifier. If we introspect, we write that ~40 lines ourselves. Not a blocker, but it must be its own bead with its own tests rather than assumed free.

`AccessToken` fields available to us (`provider.py:52-59`): `token`, `client_id`, `scopes`, `expires_at`, `resource`, `subject`, `claims`. `claims` is where `iss` lives — `principal_components` (`provider.py:62-70`) reads `claims['iss']`.

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text:
## SDK fact 6: the SDK *does* ship a working RFC 7591 DCR endpoint — but only in AS mode

`mcp/server/auth/handlers/register.py` is a complete RFC 7591 §3.1 implementation (line 33 cites the RFC by URL):

- Mints `client_id = str(uuid4())` (line 48) and `client_secret = secrets.token_hex(32)` for confidential clients (line 69).
- Defaults `token_endpoint_auth_method` to `client_secret_post` (51-52); **refuses `private_key_jwt`** (57-60) with a comment explaining it holds no client key to verify such an assertion.
- Enforces `valid_scopes` / `default_scopes` from `ClientRegistrationOptions` (71-82), returning `invalid_client_metadata` for out-of-set scopes.
- Handles `client_secret_expires_at` per RFC 7591 §3.2.1 (121-127), `0` meaning never expires.

**Crucially, the `/register` route is only mounted when an `auth_server_provider` is configured** — `create_auth_routes(...)` is called only under `if auth_server_provider:` (`lowlevel/server.py:780-790`), and within it `/register` requires `client_registration_options.enabled` (`auth/routes.py:120-134`).

### Why this matters for the decision

This is the crux of the whole choice:

- In **pure RS mode** (what we want — `token_verifier=` only), the SDK mounts *only* `/mcp` and the RFC 9728 doc. **No `/register`, no `/authorize`, no `/token`.** DCR must then come from whatever AS we point `issuer_url` at. If that AS lacks DCR, and the client requires DCR, we are stuck.
- In **AS mode** (`auth_server_provider=`), we get DCR for free but must implement the full `OAuthAuthorizationServerProvider` protocol — `provider.py:137-345` — which is ~12 methods including `authorize`, `exchange_authorization_code`, refresh-token handling and revocation, **plus** user authentication, credential storage and session security. That is a security-critical component to own for a hobby project.

Also note `register.py` has **no authentication on the endpoint** — anonymous registration, as RFC 7591 permits. Self-hosting the AS means exposing an open registration endpoint to the internet, i.e. an unauthenticated write path that mints credentials. Rate-limiting/abuse is then our problem.

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text:
## SDK fact 7 (empirical): `client_registration_options` and `revocation_options` are SILENTLY INERT in RS mode

Ran `tmp/dcr_check.py`: built `AuthSettings` with **both** `client_registration_options={'enabled': True}` and `revocation_options={'enabled': True}`, passed `token_verifier=` (no `auth_server_provider`), and listed the routes:

```
RS mode, registration+revocation ENABLED in AuthSettings:
    /mcp
    /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp
```

**No `/register`. No `/revoke`. No warning, no error.** This confirms by experiment what the code read predicted (`lowlevel/server.py:780` gates `create_auth_routes` on `auth_server_provider`).

This is a genuine footgun: someone could set `client_registration_options.enabled=True` believing they had turned DCR on, ship it, and only discover at connector-setup time that no registration endpoint exists. Worth an explicit note in `auth.py` and a test asserting the route list, so a future SDK change that starts honouring it doesn't slip past unnoticed.

**Decision-relevant restatement:** in RS mode we cannot provide DCR ourselves at all. Whether Claude.ai/ChatGPT can connect therefore depends *entirely* on the chosen AS supporting RFC 7591 — this is the single hard requirement on AS selection, not a preference.

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text:
## MAJOR REFRAME: DCR is **deprecated** in the current MCP spec; CIMD supersedes it

I verified this myself against the primary source (WebFetch of <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization>), not just via the research subagent. The task brief's premise — 'the MCP spec says clients SHOULD use DCR' — **was true of an older revision and is now out of date.**

Spec revision **2026-07-28**, §Overview, verbatim:

> 2. Authorization servers and MCP clients **SHOULD** support [OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents] ([draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document-00]).
>
> 3. Authorization servers and MCP clients **MAY** support the OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration Protocol ([RFC7591]). Note that Dynamic Client Registration **is deprecated and retained for backwards compatibility** with authorization servers that do not support Client ID Metadata Documents.

So the normative levels are now: **CIMD = SHOULD, DCR = MAY (deprecated)**. Client registration priority order is defined in the spec's Client Registration page: pre-registered → CIMD → DCR → prompt the user.

This changes the AS selection criterion materially. 'Does it do DCR' is no longer the single gate; 'does it do CIMD, or DCR as fallback' is. It also means a **pre-registered client is a first-class, spec-blessed option** (priority 1), not a second-best hack — which matters enormously for a single-maintainer hobby project.

## MUST-level requirement the SDK does NOT satisfy for us — confirms SDK fact 2

Same page, §Token Handling, verbatim:

> MCP servers, acting in their role as an OAuth 2.1 resource server, **MUST** validate access tokens as described in [OAuth 2.1 Section 5.2]. MCP servers **MUST** validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience, according to [RFC 8707 Section 2]. […] MCP servers **MUST** only accept tokens that are valid for use with their own resources. MCP servers **MUST NOT** accept or transit any other tokens.

Combined with SDK fact 2 (nothing in `bearer_auth.py` ever reads `AccessToken.resource`), this is now not merely 'good practice' but a **spec MUST that our `TokenVerifier` has to implement or we are non-compliant.** Highest-priority acceptance criterion on the verifier bead.

## Two more spec requirements we currently miss

1. **`scope` in the 401 challenge** — §Scope Selection Strategy: servers **SHOULD** include a `scope` parameter in `WWW-Authenticate`. Our prototype's 401 (SDK fact 4) emits `error`, `error_description` and `resource_metadata` but **no `scope`** — `RequireAuthMiddleware._send_auth_error` (`bearer_auth.py:113-120`) has no code path for it. A SHOULD we currently fail; needs a custom middleware or an upstream patch.
2. **403 + `insufficient_scope` for runtime scope errors** — the SDK does emit 403 `insufficient_scope` (`bearer_auth.py:106-108`), but again without the `scope=` parameter the spec asks for.

## Client-side verification (primary source)

**ChatGPT** — <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/mcp>, verbatim:
> "We recommend using OAuth with Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD) for client registration when your authorization server supports CIMD… ChatGPT supports CIMD with public-client token exchange (`none`) or signed client assertion token exchange (`private_key_jwt`)."
> "Dynamic client registration remains supported when configured."

So ChatGPT supports **both** CIMD and DCR. Good news: it does not force DCR.

**Claude.ai** — the support article only says you may *optionally* supply an OAuth Client ID and Secret under Advanced settings. **What it does NOT say** (flagging as UNVERIFIED, per the brief): whether leaving those blank triggers DCR, whether Claude.ai supports CIMD, or which grant types it drives. The docs are silent. This is the single biggest open risk and I will label it as such rather than guess.

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text:
## Client Registration page verified — DCR carries an explicit deprecation `<Warning>`

Source: <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/client-registration>

Verbatim priority order:

> Clients supporting all options **SHOULD** use the following priority order:
> 1. Use pre-registered client information for the server if the client has it available
> 2. Use Client ID Metadata Documents if the Authorization Server indicates that it supports them (via `client_id_metadata_document_supported` in OAuth Authorization Server Metadata)
> 3. Use Dynamic Client Registration as a fallback if the Authorization Server supports it (via `registration_endpoint` in OAuth Authorization Server Metadata)
> 4. Prompt the user to enter the client information if no other option is available

Verbatim deprecation warning on the DCR section:

> Dynamic Client Registration is deprecated. New implementations should use Client ID Metadata Documents instead. This option remains available for backwards compatibility with authorization servers that do not support Client ID Metadata Documents.

Verbatim on pre-registration (note this is a client-side SHOULD, i.e. clients are expected to offer the manual-credentials path):

> MCP clients **SHOULD** support an option for static client credentials such as those supplied by a pre-registration flow.

**This is what makes the Claude.ai unknown survivable.** Claude.ai's Advanced-settings 'OAuth Client ID / Client Secret' fields are exactly registration mechanism #1 (pre-registration) / #4 (prompt the user). So even in the worst case where Claude.ai supports neither CIMD nor DCR, a manually pre-registered client still connects — we just paste the ID and secret into that dialog. The recommendation therefore does **not** need to depend on Claude.ai doing DCR or CIMD, which is precisely the dependency I could not verify.

Also relevant, verbatim:
> Client IDs based on Client ID Metadata Documents are portable across authorization servers, since they are self-hosted HTTPS URLs resolved by the authorization server on demand. No re-registration is needed when the authorization server changes.

CIMD is a **client-side** capability (the client hosts the JSON doc). As an RS we neither host nor validate it — it is purely the AS's job to fetch and validate. So CIMD support is a criterion for choosing the **AS**, and costs us no implementation work.

title: OAuth 2.1 resource server for the public HTTP endpoint
description:
## Goal

Let Claude.ai and ChatGPT connect to a publicly exposed instance of this
server with a real login. This is option 3 from PLAN.md *Protecting the
HTTP endpoint*.

## Why this is needed at all

Epic lgmcp-07y deliberately scoped itself to options 1 (unguessable path)
and 2 (static bearer token) and recorded that OAuth would become "a later
epic to be created when the server is shared beyond the owner". That
condition is now in view: lgmcp-ei5.4 would advertise a remote endpoint in
the official MCP registry.

The constraint that forces OAuth, from PLAN.md and confirmed while
researching lgmcp-ei5.3:

- A static bearer token works only for clients that can send a fixed
  `Authorization` header — Claude Code `.mcp.json`, the `mcp` Python
  client, curl.
- **Claude.ai custom connectors and ChatGPT cannot send a fixed header.**
  Neither UI offers custom headers; they speak OAuth or no-auth.

So a protected remote endpoint usable from those two clients requires
OAuth. There is no cheaper path to the same outcome.

## Shape of the work

The MCP spec model is that this server is a *resource server* validating
bearer tokens issued by a **separate authorization server**, and publishing
`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`. The RS side is small — the SDK
ships `IntrospectionTokenVerifier` and an example. The real cost, and the
main open question, is which AS to use and who operates it.

## Non-goals

- Replacing the static token from lgmcp-07y.1. That stays as the mechanism
  for Claude Code and scripted clients; it is simpler and sufficient there.
- Authenticating stdio. SDK auth applies to HTTP transports only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A remote instance can be added as a custom connector in **both**
  Claude.ai and ChatGPT, completing a login flow and then answering a real
  question against live council data.
- Unauthenticated requests to the MCP endpoint get HTTP 401.
- `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` is served and correct.
- stdio and the local static-token path are both unaffected.
- PLAN.md updated to record what was chosen and why.

title: Handle upstream rate limiting in the MCP tool layer
description:
## Context

Discovered while implementing `lgmcp-7yl`, which taught the *fixture recorder* to retry 429s and honour `Retry-After`. The MCP tool layer in `src/lgsf_mcp/server.py` has **no such handling**: a 429 from upstream surfaces to the model as a bare `ToolError` reading `Council Gateway API 429: ...`, with no indication that waiting would help.

Harmless today — the [Council Gateway API](https://councilgateway.poteris.co.uk/council-api) is open and unthrottled — but this server is intended to be exposed publicly over Tailscale Funnel (`PLAN.md` *Phases → 3*), where several clients could share one upstream and trip a future limit.

`CouncilApiError` now carries `.headers` and a `.retry_after` property (added by `lgmcp-7yl`), which is exactly the input this needs.

## Task

Decide and implement one of two approaches — say which and why in a `bd` comment:

1. **Inform the model.** Map a 429 to a tool error that states the wait explicitly, e.g. `"Council Gateway API rate limit reached; retry in 12s"` using `e.retry_after`. Cheap, honest, and lets the model decide. Preferred unless retrying proves clearly better.
2. **Retry inside the tool.** Bounded retry (1–2 attempts) honouring `Retry-After`, capped well below the MCP client's own timeout so the tool does not appear to hang. Riskier: a slow tool call is worse UX than a clear error, and upstream council-wide listings already take up to ~15s.

Whichever is chosen, keep `CouncilGatewayClient` itself retry-free — that has been a deliberate decision throughout (see `lgmcp-cj6`, `lgmcp-7yl`).

## Files

- `src/lgsf_mcp/server.py` — modify: `_api_error()` and/or the shared tool error path
- `src/lgsf_mcp/client.py` — read: `CouncilApiError.retry_after`
- `tests/test_tools_*.py` — add: a 429 case asserting the model-facing message

## Dependencies

- Discovered from: `lgmcp-7yl` (Retry 429 and honour Retry-After in the fixture recorder).
- Touches `src/lgsf_mcp/server.py`, so it must not run concurrently with any tool bead.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A simulated upstream 429 produces a tool error whose message tells the model it is a rate limit and, when `Retry-After` is present, how long to wait.
2. Non-429 errors are unchanged.
3. If retry was chosen, the total tool duration stays bounded and is covered by a test that does not really sleep.
4. `uv run pytest`, `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run mypy` pass.
5. Committed with trailer `Refs: bead <this bead's id>`.
close_reason: Merged to main as 1b8da12 and verified: 186 tests pass, 10 live skipped; all four gates clean. Synthesised 429s myself — with Retry-After: 30 the model is told to wait 30 seconds and retry the same call; without it, to wait a few seconds; both say plainly it is an upstream rate limit rather than a bad request. Confirmed exactly one upstream call per tool call, so no retry was smuggled into the tool or client.

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text:
**Approach chosen (option 1, as specified in the bead): inform the model, no retry in the tool.**

Implementation plan after reading the code:

- `_api_error(e)` in `src/lgsf_mcp/server.py:138` is the single conversion point; every tool goes through `raise ToolError(_api_error(e)) from e`. Special-casing 429 there covers all tools with no per-tool changes.
- Non-429 wording `f"Council Gateway API {e.status}: {e.detail}"` must stay byte-identical — asserted by `tests/test_tools_councils.py:241,250`, `test_tools_documents.py:246`, `test_tools_misc.py:246,324`, `test_chatgpt_tools.py:255`, `test_search.py:199`.
- `CouncilApiError.retry_after` (client.py) already returns float seconds or None, handling both delta-seconds and HTTP-date. No client changes needed; client stays retry-free.
- `FixtureTransport` (tests/conftest.py) currently maps route -> `(status, body)` and **cannot attach response headers**. Extending it additively: route values may be a 2-tuple (as now) or a 3-tuple `(status, body, headers)`. Existing 2-tuple routes unaffected.

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text:
**Implemented and verified.**

Exact messages now produced:

- With `Retry-After: 30`:
  `Council Gateway API 429: Rate limit exceeded — this is an upstream rate limit, not a bug or a bad request, and the arguments were fine. Upstream asked for a 30-second wait; retry the same call with the same arguments after waiting 30 seconds. Do not rephrase the request or give up.`
- Without `Retry-After`:
  `Council Gateway API 429: Rate limit exceeded — this is an upstream rate limit, not a bug or a bad request, and the arguments were fine. No Retry-After was given; wait a few seconds, then retry the same call with the same arguments. Do not rephrase the request or give up.`
- Non-429 unchanged: `Council Gateway API 404: Not Found`

Notes for whoever comes next:

- The SDK prefixes all of this with `Error executing tool <name>: `, so the model sees the whole thing as one line of text. Kept it one paragraph for that reason.
- Duration is formatted with `:g`, so an integer `Retry-After` reads `30`, not `30.0`. An HTTP-date `Retry-After` yields a fractional value (`.retry_after` computes it against `now`), hence the regex in the HTTP-date test rather than an equality assert.
- Added a test asserting exactly **one** upstream request is made for a 429 — a guard against someone later slipping a retry into the tool or client, which `lgmcp-cj6`/`lgmcp-7yl` deliberately ruled out.
- `FixtureTransport` extension is additive: route values stay `(status, body)` or become `(status, body, headers)`; the new `Canned` type alias covers both. No existing route needed changing.

Gates: `uv run pytest` 186 passed / 10 skipped (was 182/10 — 4 new tests); `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`, `uv run mypy` all clean.

title: Usage skill teaching the council data model and query strategy
description:
## Context

Route 3 of epic lgmcp-ei5. Note this route helps a model *use* the server
well; it does nothing to help a user *connect*. It is filed under the same
epic because it ships alongside the plugin, but it must not be treated as a
substitute for the connection work.

**Scope boundary against lgmcp-s5x.** That bead puts four narrow, per-tool
gotchas into individual tool descriptions (empty /people, file 404s on
pending extracts, 600s presigned URL expiry, search total capped at 10000).
This bead is the cross-cutting strategy that fits in no single tool
description. Do not restate the four facts here; link to the tools instead.

## Why a skill is warranted

The upstream data model is genuinely unobvious, and getting it wrong
produces confidently wrong answers:

- Documents are polymorphic: `source_type` / `source_id` point at either a
  Meeting or a Decision. A model that assumes documents hang off meetings
  will miss decision documents entirely.
- Only **document text** and **document classifications** are indexed in
  OpenSearch. Meetings, decisions and people are *not* searchable — they
  must be reached by filter, or via the documents that mention them. A
  model that expects `search` to find a meeting will wrongly conclude it
  does not exist.
- Council-wide listings are slow in production (documents by council ~15s,
  `is_minutes` ~7s, key decisions ~3.5s). Prefer meeting- or
  decision-scoped listings.
- Minutes text can be very large and is windowed by `get_document`
  (`text_offset` / `max_chars`); the model must page rather than assume it
  has the whole document.

That is a multi-paragraph research strategy — too long to repeat in every
tool description, and it is about how to *sequence* tool calls.

## Task

1. Write `skills/lgsf-research/SKILL.md` with frontmatter (`name`,
   `description` naming the triggers: UK council minutes, committee
   decisions, councillors, local government meetings).
2. Body: the data model above; a worked example of the canonical loop
   (`search_council_data` -> `get_document` with windowing ->
   `get_meeting` for context); when to filter instead of search; the
   performance guidance; and the caveat that coverage is ModernGov
   councils only (~80%), so absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.
3. Decide and record where the skill is installed from: bundled in the
   Claude Code plugin (see the plugin bead), copyable into
   `~/.claude/skills/`, or both. Document it in the README.

## Dependencies

- Depends on epic lgmcp-2hd — the skill must reference real tool names and
  parameters, so the tools must exist first.
- Related to lgmcp-s5x (per-tool descriptions); keep the split above.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Asking Claude a realistic question ("what did Sheffield planning
   committee decide about X?") with the skill loaded produces a sensible
   tool sequence, verified by inspecting the actual calls made.
2. The skill contains no fact that duplicates a tool description written
   by lgmcp-s5x.
3. No blank line contains trailing whitespace.
4. Committed with trailer `Refs: bead <this bead>`.

The worked example was executed live, not written from imagination, and the agent verified mechanically that all 14 tool/parameter references in the skill match live list_tools() schemas. Skill lives at skills/lgsf-research/SKILL.md, which doubles as the plugin's own skills path, so there is one source of truth for both install routes.

comments.text:
## Live worked example ran — and surfaced three facts the brief did not have

Executed via in-memory `mcp.Client(create_server())` against the real API
(`tmp/worked_example*.py`). Confirmed **14 tools** at runtime:
`fetch, get_council, get_decision, get_document, get_document_file_url,
get_meeting, get_person, list_councils, list_decisions, list_documents,
list_meetings, list_people, search, search_council_data`.

The loop, all real output:

- `search_council_data(q='low traffic neighbourhood', size=3)` →
  `total: 340`, `total_is_capped: false`, 3 hits with `highlights`
  carrying `**Low** **Traffic** **Neighbourhood**`.
- `get_document(1199223, include_text=true, max_chars=2000)` →
  `text_length: 7703`, `has_more: true`, `next_offset: 2000`; second
  window at `text_offset=2000` → `next_offset: 4000`. Windowing works
  exactly as documented.
- `get_meeting(95384)` → Enfield 'Culture and Environment Scrutiny Panel -
  Tuesday, 11th November, 2025 7.00 pm', `council_id: 176`,
  `committee_id: 11183`.
- `get_council(176)` → Enfield, `modern_gov`, `majority_party: LAB`,
  `committees_total: 75`.

### Three new findings (worth flagging to the orchestrator)

1. **`is_minutes` under-reports badly.** Document 1199223 is
   `Printed+minutes+11th-Nov-2025...pdf` with `extract_status: success`
   and readable minutes text — yet `is_minutes: false`. Every one of the
   160 documents on that meeting had `is_minutes: false`. So
   `list_meetings(has_minutes=true)` and `list_documents(is_minutes=true)`
   are *narrowing* filters that silently drop real minutes. The tool
   descriptions for `list_documents`/`list_meetings` present `is_minutes`
   as the reliable route to readable text; live data contradicts that.
2. **`extract_status` has a third value: `failed`**, not just
   `success`/`pending`. Roughly 15 of the 160 documents on meeting 95384
   were `failed`. `get_document_file_url`'s description mentions only
   `pending` and `success`.
3. **`get_meeting.documents` is not scoped to the meeting.** Meeting 95384
   returned 160 documents spanning `created_at` from 2025-09 to 2025-12 —
   that is the committee's whole document set, not that sitting's papers.
   Also `attendees: []`, `additional_attendees: []`, `topline: None`,
   `tags: []`, `decisions: 0` on this meeting, so the 'hub record' is
   often much emptier than its description implies.

All three go into the skill as realistic caveats. Finding 1 in particular is
a correctness trap: a model told to trust `is_minutes` will conclude a
council published no minutes when it did.

comments.text:
## Party trap, filter path and coverage all verified live

### Party counting — the trap is worse than the tool description says

`list_people` `total` values, each a separate live call:

| filter | total |
| --- | --- |
| (none) | **19745** |
| `party="Conservative"` | 3089 |
| `party="Conservative Party"` | 337 |
| `party="The Conservative Party"` | 167 |
| `party="Local Conservatives"` | 125 |
| `party="Labour"` | 3573 |
| `party="Labour Party"` | 704 |

So the four Conservative spellings I tried already sum to 3718 vs the 3089 a
naive `party=Conservative` reports — a 20% undercount, and that is only the
spellings I guessed.

**27 distinct `party` values appear in a single page of 100 people**,
including `Labour`, `Labour Party`, `Labour and Co-operative`,
`Labour and Co-operative Party`, `Labour & Co-operative`,
`Labour & Cooperative Party` (six Labour spellings), and `Liberal Democrat`,
`Liberal Democrats`, `(Liberal Democrats)`,
`Scottish Liberal Democrat Party`. Also note `Reform UK` was the single most

`list_councils` totals: **320** overall, **289** `modern_gov`, **31** `cmis`.
So the ~80% ModernGov figure is about which *UK* councils are scraped at all,
not the modern_gov/cmis split within the 320.

`list_meetings(council_id=176, committee_id=11183, date_from="2025-11-01",

`additional_attendees` "are populated". I sampled four meetings across two

`attendees: []` and `additional_attendees: []`**, plus `topline: None`. Two
of the three Aberdeen meetings had zero documents too (they are future-dated,

`list_decisions` warns).

I cannot verify from four samples that attendees are *never* populated, so
the skill says "often empty — do not rely on it; read the minutes text for
who attended" rather than claiming they are always empty.

title: Distribution: make connecting to the server easy
description:
## Goal

Today the only way to use this server is: clone the repo, `uv sync`, then
hand-write an `.mcp.json` containing an absolute path to the checkout.
That is too much friction for anyone who is not the maintainer. This epic
makes connecting as close to one step as possible, for both local and
remote deployments.

## Two deployment modes

The server already supports both (`--transport stdio|streamable-http`),
and the distribution routes split along that line:

| Mode | Transport | Who runs it | How a user connects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Local (default) | stdio | the user | `uvx lgsf-mcp` |
| Local HTTP | streamable-http on 127.0.0.1 | the user | local URL as connector |
| Remote | streamable-http on a public URL | the maintainer | URL as custom connector |

## Routes, cheapest first

1. **PyPI + uvx** — turns the `.mcp.json` command into `uvx lgsf-mcp`, with
   no clone and no absolute path, and enables
   `claude mcp add lgsf -- uvx lgsf-mcp`. Local mode only; remote users
   install nothing. Prerequisite for routes 2 and 4.
2. **Claude Code plugin + marketplace** — `/plugin install` wires the
   server up with zero JSON editing, and can bundle the usage skill.
3. **Usage skill** — orthogonal to connecting: teaches the data model
   rather than the install. Transport-agnostic.
4. **Official MCP registry** — discoverability beyond Claude Code, and the
   one route that can advertise the package and a remote endpoint together.

## Constraints

- Nothing here is publishable until epic lgmcp-2hd (Phase 2 tools) lands;
  there is no useful tool surface to distribute before then.
- A genuinely public **remote** deployment is gated on epic lgmcp-07y.
  Per PLAN.md, the static bearer token (option 2) cannot be sent by
  Claude.ai or ChatGPT; only OAuth (option 3) works for those clients. So
  advertising a remote endpoint publicly implies doing the OAuth work
  first, or accepting an unauthenticated endpoint.
- README usage docs are already covered by lgmcp-o2q.2 — these beads must
  extend that section, not duplicate it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new user can connect to a local server with a single command that
  contains no filesystem path.
- The README states plainly which routes exist and which deployment mode
  each one serves.
notes:
SCOPE CHANGE 2026-08-23. Adam decided against PyPI for now, so the epic
premise has shifted and the whole thing drops in priority.

- lgmcp-ei5.1 (PyPI) — DEFERRED, P4. Alpha; maintenance burden; and uvx
  installs from a git URL anyway, which already removes the clone and the
  absolute path that motivated it.
- lgmcp-ei5.4 (MCP registry) — DEFERRED, P4. Needs the PyPI README marker
  for ownership, and is the most "invite strangers" route of the four.
- lgmcp-ei5.3 (plugin + marketplace) — P4, PyPI dependency cut, rewritten
  to install from a git URL.
- lgmcp-ei5.2 (usage skill) — CLOSED and shipped. The one route that
  delivered value without publishing anything.

Real blocker now: **there is no public git remote.** Confirmed — git has no
origin. Every remaining route needs one, so that decision comes first.

The epic acceptance criterion "a new user can connect with a single command
containing no filesystem path" is still achievable without PyPI, via
`uvx --from git+<url> lgsf-mcp`.

title: Decide on ruff format as a quality gate
description:
## Context

Discovered while implementing `lgmcp-87u`. `uv run ruff format --check .` currently fails on two files, and this is **pre-existing** — verified by stashing that bead's diff and re-running, which reported the identical offenders.

Every bead's acceptance criteria say "`uv run ruff check .` passes", which does **not** imply formatting is clean: `check` (lint) and `format` are separate ruff modes. So formatting is drifting unchecked while looking green.

## Task

Decide and implement one of:

1. **Adopt it** — run `uv run ruff format .`, commit the reformat as one isolated commit, and add `uv run ruff format --check .` to the standard gate list in `AGENTS.md` so later beads include it.
2. **Reject it** — record in `AGENTS.md` that the project lints but does not auto-format, so nobody re-raises this.

Option 1 is the conventional choice with ruff and keeps diffs stable, but the reformat touches shared files, so land it when no sibling worktree is editing them.

## Files

- `src/lgsf_mcp/client.py` — reformat (the `_get` signature around line 102 would collapse to one line)
- `scripts/record_fixtures.py` — reformat
- `AGENTS.md` — modify: record the decision either way
- `pyproject.toml` — read: `[tool.ruff]` already sets `line-length = 88`

## Dependencies

- Discovered from: `lgmcp-87u` (Expose public is_closed on CouncilGatewayClient).
- Best landed while no other bead is mid-flight on `client.py`, to avoid conflicts.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `uv run ruff format --check .` passes, **or** `AGENTS.md` explicitly records that formatting is not gated.
2. If adopted, the reformat is its own commit, separate from any behaviour change.
3. `uv run pytest`, `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run mypy` still pass.
4. Committed with trailer `Refs: bead <this bead's id>`.

title: Set serverInfo.version from package metadata
description:
## Context

Discovered while implementing `lgmcp-2hd.1` (Server core). `MCPServer` defaults `version: str = ""` and `create_server()` passes none, so the MCP handshake advertises an empty version string. Confirmed live: `serverInfo` in the `initialize` response carries `"name":"lgsf-mcp"` but no meaningful version.

Clients display this, and it makes bug reports ambiguous once the server is exposed publicly (see `PLAN.md` *Phases → 3*).

## Task

In `src/lgsf_mcp/server.py`, pass a real version to `MCPServer`, read from package metadata:

```python
from importlib.metadata import version
MCPServer(name=SERVER_NAME, version=version("lgsf-mcp"), ...)
```

Handle `PackageNotFoundError` by falling back to `"0.0.0+unknown"` so a source checkout without an install still starts.

Add a test asserting the initialize handshake reports a non-empty version matching `pyproject.toml`.

## Files

- `src/lgsf_mcp/server.py` — modify: pass `version=` to `MCPServer`
- `tests/test_server.py` — modify: assert non-empty `serverInfo.version`

## Dependencies

- Discovered from: `lgmcp-2hd.1` (Server core: MCPServer factory and CLI).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The `initialize` response's `serverInfo.version` equals the version in `pyproject.toml`.
2. Server still starts from a source checkout when the package is not installed.
3. `uv run pytest`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run mypy` pass.
4. Committed with trailer `Refs: bead <this bead's id>`.
close_reason: Merged to main as e1f25b6 and verified: 182 tests pass, 10 live skipped; ruff check, ruff format --check (27 files) and mypy (22 files) clean. Confirmed on the wire — a real streamable-http server's initialize response returns serverInfo {'name': 'lgsf-mcp', 'version': '0.1.0'}, matching pyproject.toml, where it was previously an empty string.

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text: Un-dispatched by the orchestrator before any work started: this edits src/lgsf_mcp/server.py, which lgmcp-2hd.3 is concurrently rewriting. Deferred to run after the server.py tool beads land, to avoid a guaranteed merge conflict.

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text:
## Implemented on branch `bgp/lgmcp-06q`

**Confirmed the diagnosis directly** rather than trusting it: `inspect.signature(MCPServer.__init__)` shows `version` as a keyword param defaulting to `""`, sitting alongside `name`/`title`/`description`/`instructions`. So the empty-version report was accurate.

### Design notes for the next reader

- `_server_version()` is a **function called inside `create_server()`**, not a module-level constant. That is deliberate: a module-level `VERSION = ...` would be evaluated once at import, before any test could monkeypatch it, making the `PackageNotFoundError` fallback untestable without reimporting the module. Please do not "simplify" it into a constant.
- The fallback string is exported as `UNKNOWN_VERSION = "0.0.0+unknown"` so the test asserts against the same symbol the source uses, rather than a duplicated literal.
- The test reads the expected version via `importlib.metadata.version("lgsf-mcp")`, not a hardcoded `"0.1.0"`, so a version bump in `pyproject.toml` will not break it.

### Monkeypatch target — a real trap

`monkeypatch.setattr` must target **`lgsf_mcp.server.version`** (the name as bound into the server module by `from importlib.metadata import ... version`), *not* `importlib.metadata.version`. Patching the latter would not affect the already-bound reference in `server.py`. The test imports the module as `server_module` purely to give the patch a target.

### Verification that the tests are load-bearing

I mutation-tested rather than just observing green: temporarily removed the `version=_server_version(),` line from `MCPServer(...)` and re-ran — **both new tests failed**; restored, both pass. So they genuinely pin the behaviour and are not vacuous.

Fallback specifically verified by monkeypatching `version()` to raise `PackageNotFoundError`, then completing a full `initialize` handshake through the in-memory `Client` and asserting `server_info.version == "0.0.0+unknown"`. The server starts and handshakes normally, satisfying AC2.

### Accessor

Client-side the SDK exposes snake_case `client.server_info.version` (there is no `serverInfo` attribute) — consistent with the existing `test_initialize_and_instructions`, which already used `client.server_info.name`.

### Gates
`uv run pytest` → 182 passed, 10 skipped (180 pre-existing + my 2). `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy` (strict) all clean. No trailing whitespace.

## Upstream /people data facts (verified live, for tool descriptions)

The orchestrator owns `src/lgsf_mcp/server.py`; these are the facts its

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text:
Implementation note — **do not use a pytest fixture to hold the MCP `Client`** in async tests.

First version wrapped `async with Client(create_server())` in an `@pytest.fixture`. Result: `10 passed, 10 errors` — every test passed and then blew up in teardown with

RuntimeError: Attempted to exit cancel scope in a different task than it was entered in

title: Retry 429 and honour Retry-After in the fixture recorder
description:
## Context

Discovered while implementing `lgmcp-cj6`. The retry predicate `is_transient()` in `scripts/record_fixtures.py` treats only 5xx and `httpx.TransportError` as transient, so **429 Too Many Requests is not retried** and the `Retry-After` header is ignored.

Harmless today — the [Council Gateway API](https://councilgateway.poteris.co.uk/council-api) is open and unthrottled — but wrong the moment upstream adds rate limiting, and the recorder makes ~16 sequential live calls per run so it is exactly the client that would trip a limit.

## Task

In `scripts/record_fixtures.py`:

1. Extend `is_transient()` to treat HTTP 429 as transient.
2. When the response carries `Retry-After`, wait that long instead of the exponential backoff. Support both forms in the header (delta-seconds and an HTTP-date). Cap the honoured wait at something sane (say 60s) so a hostile or mistaken header cannot hang the run.
3. `CouncilApiError` currently exposes `.status` and `.detail` but not headers, so surfacing `Retry-After` needs either a small addition to `src/lgsf_mcp/client.py` or for the recorder to catch at a lower level. Prefer adding `.headers` (or a `.retry_after` property) to `CouncilApiError` — it is generally useful and keeps the recorder simple. Say which you chose and why in a bead comment.

## Files

- `scripts/record_fixtures.py` — modify: `is_transient()` and the backoff computation
- `src/lgsf_mcp/client.py` — likely modify: expose response headers on `CouncilApiError`
- `tests/test_record_fixtures.py` — modify: cover 429-with-`Retry-After`, 429-without, and the cap

## Dependencies

- Discovered from: `lgmcp-cj6` (Retry transient upstream 500s in the fixture recorder).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A simulated 429 is retried; with `Retry-After: 2` the wait is 2s, not the exponential value.
2. An absurd `Retry-After` (e.g. 86400) is capped rather than honoured.
3. A 429 with no `Retry-After` falls back to exponential backoff.
4. Existing 5xx / 4xx behaviour is unchanged — verify by setting `RETRY_ATTEMPTS = 1` and confirming exactly the retry-dependent tests fail, then restoring.
5. `uv run pytest`, `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run mypy` pass.
6. Committed with trailer `Refs: bead <this bead's id>`.
close_reason: Merged to main as d5f7852 and verified: 117 tests pass, ruff and mypy (17 files) clean. Directly checked the semantics — 429 and 500 transient, 404 not; Retry-After: 2 gives 2.0s; 86400 caps at 60.0s; no header falls back to exponential 1.0s; HTTP-date +30s parses to ~29s and a past date to 0.0s.

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text:
## Design decision: `.headers` + `.retry_after` on `CouncilApiError`

Chose the bead's preferred option — extend `CouncilApiError` rather than have the
recorder catch at a lower level.

**Why:**

- `CouncilApiError` has exactly one construction site (`CouncilGatewayClient._get`,
  src/lgsf_mcp/client.py:115) and the `httpx.Response` is in scope there, so
  attaching headers is a one-line change with no call-site churn.
- Catching lower down would mean either the recorder wrapping httpx directly
  (duplicating `_get`'s error-body parsing) or the client growing a retry hook —
  both worse than a data-only addition. The bead requires
  `CouncilGatewayClient` stay retry-free, which this respects: the error just
  carries more information, no behaviour change.
- `headers` defaults to `None` so the four existing `CouncilApiError(status, detail)`
  constructions in tests/test_record_fixtures.py keep working unchanged.

Adding both: `.headers` (raw, generally useful — Retry-After is not the only header
worth surfacing) and `.retry_after` (a parsed `float | None`, so the parsing lives
next to the data rather than in the recorder). The 60s cap stays in the recorder,
since it is a policy decision about *this* client's tolerance, not a property of
the error.

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text:
## Mutation check (AC 5): existing 5xx/4xx behaviour unchanged

Set `RETRY_ATTEMPTS = 1` in scripts/record_fixtures.py and ran `uv run pytest -q`:
**15 failed, 90 passed** — every failure in `tests/test_record_fixtures.py`, none
elsewhere. The 15 are exactly the retry-dependent tests (5 pre-existing + 10 new).

Crucially still passing under the mutation, which is what makes it a useful check:

- `test_4xx_is_not_retried[404]`, `[422]`
- `test_error_detail_does_not_retry_expected_4xx`
- `test_is_transient` (all 7 params, incl. the new 429/400 ones)
- the whole 41-test `tests/test_client.py` suite

So the 4xx no-retry path and the predicate are genuinely independent of the retry
count, and the new 429 handling did not perturb them. Restored to 3; full suite
green again (105 passed).

## Notes for the next person

- `backoff_delay(exc, attempt)` was extracted from the inline expression in
  `retry()` so the delay policy is directly unit-testable without a transport.
- Retry-After is honoured on **any** `CouncilApiError` that carries it, not just
  429 — RFC 9110 permits it on 503 too, and there is no reason to ignore a
  server's own estimate. Covered by `test_retry_after_on_a_503_is_also_honoured`.
- `RETRY_BACKOFF * 2 ** (attempt - 1)` had to become
  `RETRY_BACKOFF * float(2 ** (attempt - 1))`: once it sat in a function declared
  `-> float`, mypy strict flagged `no-any-return` on the int-power expression.
- Tests never really sleep — the pre-existing autouse `no_sleep` fixture patches
  `recorder.asyncio.sleep` and appends to `SLEPT`, so the 86400s and 60s cases
  are instant.

title: List in the official MCP registry (package + optional remote)
description:
## Context

Route 4 of epic lgmcp-ei5. Discoverability beyond Claude Code, and the
**only** route that can advertise a remote endpoint — a plugin `.mcp.json`
cannot (see lgmcp-ei5.3). One registry entry may carry both a `packages[]`
entry and a `remotes[]` entry, letting clients pick local or remote.

Docs: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/registry/quickstart.md,
https://modelcontextprotocol.io/registry/package-types.md,
https://modelcontextprotocol.io/registry/remote-servers.md
Re-verify the schema URL and field names against these before writing —
the schema is dated (`2025-12-11` at time of research) and may have moved.

## Verified shape

    {
      "$schema": "https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/2025-12-11/server.schema.json",
      "name": "io.github.aspiers/lgsf-mcp",
      "description": "Query UK local government data ...",
      "version": "0.1.0",
      "repository": {"url": "...", "source": "github"},
      "packages": [
        {"registryType": "pypi", "identifier": "lgsf-mcp", "version": "0.1.0",
         "transport": {"type": "stdio"},
         "environmentVariables": [
           {"name": "COUNCIL_API_TOKEN", "isRequired": false, "isSecret": true},
           {"name": "COUNCIL_API_URL", "isRequired": false}
         ]}
      ]
    }

Ownership of the `io.github.<user>/` namespace is proved by GitHub device-flow
auth. Ownership of the PyPI package is proved by putting an HTML comment
`<!-- mcp-name: io.github.aspiers/lgsf-mcp -->` in the README that ships to
PyPI; the value must match `name` exactly.

## Task

1. Add the `mcp-name` HTML comment to README.md (it must survive into the
   PyPI long_description — verify in the built wheel METADATA).
2. Create `server.json` via `mcp-publisher init`, then fill it in.
3. Install the `mcp-publisher` CLI, `mcp-publisher login github`, and
   `mcp-publisher publish`.
4. **Remote entry — conditional.** Only add a `remotes[]` entry once there
   is a durable public URL AND the auth question is settled. Per PLAN.md
   and epic lgmcp-07y, a static bearer token cannot be sent by Claude.ai or
   ChatGPT; only OAuth works for them. A Tailscale Funnel URL is a test
   endpoint, not a service — do NOT publish it to a public registry.
   If the remote is deferred, publish `packages[]` only and note why.
5. Confirm the entry resolves in the registry after publishing.

## Dependencies

- Depends on lgmcp-ei5.1 (PyPI) — the package must exist and carry the
  `mcp-name` marker.
- Any remote entry additionally depends on epic lgmcp-07y (endpoint auth).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The server is findable in the official registry by name.
2. Wheel METADATA contains the `mcp-name` comment.
3. Either a remote is published against a stable authenticated URL, or the
   bead records explicitly that remote listing was deferred and why.
4. Committed with trailer `Refs: bead <this bead>`.

title: Claude Code plugin + marketplace for zero-config install
description:
## Context

Route 2 of epic lgmcp-ei5. Lets a Claude Code user run `/plugin install`
and get the MCP server wired up with no JSON editing, and bundles the usage
skill (lgmcp-ei5.2) in the same install.

**Important limitation, verified against
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference.md:** a plugin `.mcp.json`
supports **local stdio servers only** (`command` + `args`). There is no way
to point a plugin at a remote HTTP/SSE URL. Remote deployments must be
advertised via the MCP registry `remotes[]` array instead (see the registry
bead). Do not attempt a remote plugin; it is not supported.

## Verified layout

Docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins.md

    <plugin-root>/
      .claude-plugin/
        plugin.json          # ONLY this file goes in .claude-plugin/
      .mcp.json              # at plugin ROOT, not inside .claude-plugin/
      skills/
        lgsf-research/
          SKILL.md

`plugin.json` requires only `name`; optional `displayName`, `description`,
`version`, `author`, `homepage`, `repository`, `license`, `keywords`,
`mcpServers`, `defaultEnabled`, `userConfig`.

`.mcp.json` supports the placeholders `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`,
`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` and `${user_config.KEY}`.

## Task

1. Decide how the plugin invokes the server, and record why. Preferred:
   `{"command": "uvx", "args": ["lgsf-mcp"]}`, which needs no bundled
   binary and reuses the PyPI release. Confirm `uvx` is an acceptable
   `command` in practice by testing, not by assuming.
2. Add `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and a root `.mcp.json`.
3. Expose `COUNCIL_API_URL` and `COUNCIL_API_TOKEN` through `userConfig` /
   `${user_config.KEY}` so a user can point at a local gateway without
   editing files. Verify the `userConfig` schema against the reference
   before writing it.
4. Bundle the skill from lgmcp-ei5.2 under `skills/`.
5. Add `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` so the repo is itself a
   marketplace, letting users run:
       /plugin marketplace add <this repo>
       /plugin install lgsf-mcp@<marketplace-name>
   Marketplace manifest needs `name`, `owner`, `plugins[]` (each with
   `name`, `source`, `description`, `version`).
6. Run `claude plugin validate` locally.
7. Document the install in the README alongside the other routes.

## Out of scope

Submitting to the official public directory
(https://platform.claude.com/plugins/submit) reportedly requires a
Team/Enterprise org. File a separate bead if that is wanted.

## Dependencies

- Depends on lgmcp-ei5.1 (PyPI) if the `uvx` command is used.
- Depends on lgmcp-ei5.2 (skill) for the bundled skill.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `/plugin marketplace add` + `/plugin install` against a clean Claude Code
   profile yields a working server whose tools are listed, with no manual
   JSON editing at any point.
2. The bundled skill is invocable as `/lgsf-mcp:lgsf-research`.
3. `claude plugin validate` passes.
4. README states plainly that the plugin serves local stdio only.
5. Committed with trailer `Refs: bead <this bead>`.
notes:
REVISED 2026-08-23. The PyPI dependency is cut — lgmcp-ei5.1 is deferred
(alpha, maintenance burden, and largely redundant given git install).

Step 1 of the task says the preferred command is `{"command": "uvx",
"args": ["lgsf-mcp"]}`, reusing a PyPI release. Use a git URL instead:

    {"command": "uvx",
     "args": ["--from", "git+<repo-url>", "lgsf-mcp"]}

This still needs no clone, no absolute path and no bundled binary, so the
zero-config goal is intact. Verify by testing, not assumption — in
particular whether uvx resolves a git URL fast enough for a plugin start,
since it clones on first run.

**Prerequisite that does not exist yet: a public git remote.** This
repository has none (bd reports no Dolt remote, and git has no origin), so
neither the git-URL install nor the marketplace `source` can be written
until one exists. That is the real blocker for this bead now, not PyPI.

title: Publish to PyPI so install is 'uvx lgsf-mcp'
description:
## Context

Route 1 of epic lgmcp-ei5, and the prerequisite for the plugin and registry
routes. Removes the clone-and-hardcode-a-path step from the install.

Before:

    {"mcpServers": {"lgsf": {"command": "uv",
      "args": ["run", "--directory", "/path/to/lgsf-mcp", "lgsf-mcp"]}}}

After:

    {"mcpServers": {"lgsf": {"command": "uvx", "args": ["lgsf-mcp"]}}}

or simply `claude mcp add lgsf -- uvx lgsf-mcp`, with no JSON editing.

Packaging is already most of the way there: hatchling build backend, `src/`
layout, `py.typed`, and a `lgsf-mcp` console script entry point.

Applies to **local** deployments only — remote users connect to a URL and
install nothing.

## Task

1. Check the name `lgsf-mcp` is free on PyPI before anything else. If taken,
   stop and raise it — do not silently pick a different name.
2. Fill in the `[project]` metadata needed for a good PyPI page: `authors`,
   `keywords`, `classifiers`, and `[project.urls]` (Homepage, Repository,
   Issues). Do not add a `License ::` classifier — PEP 639 metadata comes
   from lgmcp-c7y.
3. Set up publishing via **PyPI Trusted Publishing** (OIDC from GitHub
   Actions), not a long-lived API token. Follow
   https://docs.pypi.org/trusted-publishers/ — verify the current setup
   steps there rather than working from memory.
4. Add `.github/workflows/release.yml`: on a `v*` tag, `uv build` then
   publish. Confirm the correct publish action and its inputs against
   current docs before writing it.
5. Do a full dry run to TestPyPI first, then install from TestPyPI into a
   clean temp dir with `uvx` and confirm the server starts.
6. Extend the README *Usage* section written by lgmcp-o2q.2 with the `uvx`
   install as the primary path, keeping the from-source path as the
   contributor route.

## Dependencies

- Depends on lgmcp-c7y (licence metadata) — PyPI needs it.
- Depends on epic lgmcp-2hd (Phase 2 tools) — nothing worth shipping before
  the tools exist.
- Blocks the plugin and registry beads.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `uvx lgsf-mcp --help` works in a clean environment with no checkout
   present.
2. `claude mcp add lgsf -- uvx lgsf-mcp` produces a working server that
   lists its tools in Claude Code.
3. Tagging `v0.1.0` publishes to PyPI via CI with no manually held secret.
4. README shows the `uvx` route first.
5. Committed with trailer `Refs: bead <this bead>`.
notes:
DEFERRED 2026-08-23 by Adam. Three reasons, in his words:

1. **Not ready to be public.** The server is alpha and the upstream data is
   uneven; a PyPI listing invites users before he wants them.
2. **Maintenance burden.** Publishing implies support, issues and keeping
   releases current for strangers.
3. **Redundant given git install.** uvx installs straight from a git URL, so
   PyPI mostly buys a shorter command:

       {"mcpServers": {"lgsf": {"command": "uvx", "args":
         ["--from", "git+<repo-url>", "lgsf-mcp"]}}}

   That already removes the clone and the absolute path, which was the whole
   reason this bead was rated P2 in the first place.

Note the packaging work is NOT wasted: lgmcp-c7y (AGPL-3.0 licence and PEP
639 metadata) is done and lgmcp-owr (authors, project URLs) stands on its
own merits — both are good hygiene for a git-installable package.

What would change this decision: wanting the MCP registry listing
(lgmcp-ei5.4 verifies ownership through a PyPI README marker), or the
project reaching a point where strangers using it is the goal rather than a
risk. A public git remote is a prerequisite either way and does not exist
yet.

title: Retry transient upstream 500s in the fixture recorder
description:
## Context

Discovered while recording fixtures for `lgmcp-clg.3`: one re-record hit a transient `500 Internal Server Error` from upstream; the next attempt succeeded and produced byte-identical output. Right now a single blip aborts the whole recording run.

## Task

Add bounded retry with backoff to `scripts/record_fixtures.py` — retry on 5xx and on `httpx.TransportError`, e.g. 3 attempts with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s), logging each retry to stderr. Do **not** retry 4xx: the recorder deliberately captures a 422 and a 404 as fixtures.

Keep the retry in the script only. `CouncilGatewayClient` stays retry-free unless a separate bead decides otherwise.

## Files

- `scripts/record_fixtures.py` — modify: wrap each recording call in the retry helper

## Dependencies

- Discovered from: `lgmcp-clg.3`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A simulated 500 (e.g. via a temporary `MockTransport` in a scratch script) is retried and then succeeds.
2. A 422 or 404 is **not** retried — the recorder still captures `validation_422.json` and the person 404 in one pass.
3. `uv run python scripts/record_fixtures.py` still regenerates all fixtures identically.
4. `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run mypy` pass.
5. Committed with trailer `Refs: bead <this bead's id>`.
close_reason: Merged to main as ff4e642 and verified: 80 tests pass, ruff and mypy (16 files) clean. Independently mutation-tested by setting RETRY_ATTEMPTS=1 — exactly the 5 retry-dependent tests failed while the 4xx no-retry tests stayed green, then restored. Retry covers 5xx and TransportError; 4xx (the recorded 422 and 404) are not retried.

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text:
Design note: the script's calls are structured as `await client.foo(...)` — bare coroutines. A coroutine can only be awaited once, so a retry helper **cannot** take an `Awaitable`; it must take a zero-arg callable factory that constructs a fresh coroutine per attempt.

This also forces a signature change to the existing `error_detail(awaitable, expect)` helper -> `error_detail(call, expect)` where `call` is `Callable[[], Awaitable[object]]`. Call sites become `lambda: client.get_person(person_id)`.

Retry predicate: `CouncilApiError` exposes `.status`, so 5xx = `exc.status >= 500`; `httpx.TransportError` is the base class for connect/read/write/pool timeouts and network errors, so catching it covers the transport cases. 4xx falls through un-retried, which is what `error_detail` needs for the deliberate 422/404 fixtures.

comments.author: Adam Spiers
comments.text:
Verification evidence:

- `uv run python scripts/record_fixtures.py` against live upstream: all 16 fixtures rewritten, `git status` clean for `tests/fixtures/` afterwards -> byte-identical. AC3 met. No 5xx occurred during this run, so the retry path was not exercised live — hence the simulated-failure tests below.
- **Mutation check** (proves the tests are not vacuous): temporarily capped the retry loop to a single attempt and re-ran; exactly the 5 retry-dependent tests failed (`test_500_is_retried_then_succeeds`, `test_backoff_is_exponential_and_bounded`, `test_gives_up_after_three_attempts`, `test_transport_error_is_retried`, `test_error_detail_retries_5xx_before_the_expected_error`) while the 4xx no-retry tests stayed green. Restored afterwards.
- `uv run pytest`: 65 passed. `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run mypy` (strict, 15 files): clean.

Gotcha worth keeping: ruff's UP047 rejects the `TypeVar`-based generic here — had to use PEP 695 `async def retry[T](...)`, which is fine on the project's Python >= 3.12 floor.

comments.text:
Implemented on branch `bgp/lgmcp-cj6`, commit `ff4e642` (not pushed; orchestrator merges).

Files: `scripts/record_fixtures.py` (modified), `tests/test_record_fixtures.py` (new, 15 tests). Confirmed no overlap with the concurrently-edited `server.py`/`search.py`/`test_tools_councils.py`, and `tests/conftest.py` was not modified.

One follow-up for the orchestrator to file if wanted: `retry()` catches `Exception` and delegates to `is_transient()`, so a non-transient error still propagates on the first attempt — but if upstream ever starts returning 429, it is currently treated as non-transient (4xx) and will not be retried nor honour `Retry-After`. title: Phase 4: semantic search (future)
description:
## Goal

Add vector/semantic search so the model can find relevant minutes by meaning, not only by OpenSearch phrase match.

## Plan

Based on `PLAN.md`, section *Phases → 4. Semantic search (future)*. Not in scope yet; no child beads. Create them once the open questions are settled.

## Design hooks already in place (from Phase 2)

- `src/lgsf_mcp/search.py` defines a `SearchBackend` protocol with one implementation (`TextSearchBackend` → `/search`).
- `search_council_data` will gain a `method` parameter (`text` | `semantic` | `hybrid`, default `text`).
- Every hit carries `document_id` so `get_document` works regardless of backend.

## Open questions

1. Where do embeddings live? (a) upstream [`poteris/council-api`](https://github.com/poteris/council-api) adds `/search?mode=semantic` and this server stays thin — preferred; (b) this server builds its own index (pgvector / LanceDB / Chroma) by paging `/documents?is_minutes=true` with `include_text=true`.
2. Chunking: per agenda item vs fixed-size with overlap; store `document_id` + char offsets so `get_document(text_offset=…)` can jump to the match.
3. Embedding model: local (`bge-small`, `nomic-embed`) vs hosted. Corpus ≈ 1.59M documents; measure the minutes subset via `/documents?is_minutes=true` `total` first.
4. Hybrid ranking: reciprocal rank fusion over text + vector.

## Acceptance Criteria

Defined when child beads are created.
